paired_world_argument.scope: two CLEAN workers, non-commutative conflicting effect, no cross-role runtime observation, no sink-side old-epoch rejection
paired_world_argument.crash_world: designated owner has stopped; backup observes only its own local state plus static sanitized control
paired_world_argument.slow_world: designated owner is delayed and later resumes; backup has the same allowed observations as in crash world until its finite takeover point
paired_world_argument.result: A finite-time takeover rule that makes progress in the crash world also authorizes the backup in the indistinguishable slow world. When the old owner later acts, duplicate/conflicting/stale authority is possible unless the effect algebra makes concurrency harmless or an authoritative sink/shared fence rejects one side.
paired_world_argument.model_slice: static no-failover has 144/144 non-commutative owner-crash cases with no finite progress; timeout takeover has 144/144 corresponding slow-late non-commutative cases unsafe
paired_world_argument.scope_guard: This is a finite-model indistinguishability argument for the stated observation/effect assumptions, not a universal distributed-computing impossibility theorem.

mechanism_classification.coordination_free_static_owner: can preserve exclusivity only by sacrificing crash failover; generation/membership changes still need stale-owner rejection if old work may resume
mechanism_classification.same_effect_durable_idempotency: removes duplicate retry for the same stable effect ID but does not serialize different conflicting effect IDs or reject a stale generation
mechanism_classification.conflict_key_epoch_fenced_sink: generic positive mechanism: atomically validate conflict-key current epoch/generation and consume durable effect ID at effect application; safe/live in tested finite lattice
mechanism_classification.strict_role_local_partition: current CLEAN-compatible restricted class for disjoint role-local effects; safe/live in all 216 disjoint scenarios but deliberately fail-closes 432 same/conflicting-effect scenarios, so it is not full parity
mechanism_classification.branch_nonforce_conflict: storage serialization only; sequential retry can still apply semantic duplicate/conflicting effects, and all 216 unbounded-interference scenarios retain starvation-unproven

public_source_observations.observation: Kafka protocol exposes producer_epoch and documents broker checking it against the current epoch, rejecting mismatches; this is a concrete authoritative-sink fencing precedent, not an accepted hosted dependency for this Phase-1 route
GitHub non-force ref update requires a fast-forward and can return 409 Conflict, which prevents overwriting branch work but does not by itself define semantic effect conflict/idempotency

clean_boundary_assessment.arbitrary_external_authoritative_sink: unresolved and not accepted; a Kafka-like broker is mechanism precedent only and would introduce an external hosted coordination dependency
clean_boundary_assessment.current_policy_compatible_restricted_rou: strict disjoint role-local namespaces only; does not cover same/conflicting cross-role effects or wide-operation parity
clean_boundary_assessment.general_safety_plus_finite_failover_unde: not achieved by any tested current-policy-compatible strategy

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.public_external_systems: mechanism analogies only, never accepted dependencies
zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.repository_rate_limits: bounded interruption/recovery dimension; no rate-limit event is treated as authority revocation or proof of another worker's state

unresolved_minimal_capability.statement: For non-commutative cross-role effects that require finite failover, the tested designs need an authority point observable at effect time: either a CLEAN-authorized shared fence/epoch or an authoritative sink that atomically rejects stale/conflicting epochs and deduplicates effect IDs. Current frozen CLEAN policy exposes neither as a role-authorized general cross-role surface.

exact_continuation: Next leaf: coordination-free algebraic redesign. Test whether the unresolved cross-role fence can be removed for useful subclasses by converting effects into monotonic/idempotent/commutative contributions or statically escrowed disjoint rights that each role can publish only inside its own namespace. Compare grow-only set/join-semilattice contribution, content-addressed immutable contribution, static escrow partition, deterministic single-owner no-failover, and a fenced shared sink baseline. Include duplicate replay, conflicting payload under same semantic key, owner crash, late old owner, role add, generation supersession, and the need for a final reducer. Treat any reducer that must read other-worker state or any external merge service as a new unresolved child; target the largest outcome class that is truly executable inside current CLEAN boundaries.
